subject.title: fix: workflow sanity audit passes on main

question: Should both the primary and fallback GitHub App tokens retain `contents: read` because either may be passed to `actions/labeler` to load `.github/labeler.yml`?
rationale: The implementation and hosted proof establish that the scope fixes the current automation path, but accepting repository-content access for both App identities is an intentional security-boundary choice that cannot be inferred from code alone.

options.title: Accept the narrow content-read scope
options.body: Approve the two explicit read grants because both fallback paths can provide the token used to load the repository labeler configuration.

options.title: Use a different configuration path
options.body: Redesign labeler configuration loading so the App tokens do not require repository-content access, accepting a broader workflow change and new proof burden.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow content-read scope
recommendation.body: Approve the two explicit read grants because both fallback paths can provide the token used to load the repository labeler configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the current permission rationale and implemented the least-privilege split during this review cycle.
